name: MSX
description: MSX is a standardised home computer design announced in 1983 by ASCII Corporation and Microsoft Japan, led by Kazuhiko Nishi. Many manufacturers built compatible machines, and it was popular in Japan, South Korea, the Netherlands, Spain and Brazil. Konami's cartridges made it an important games platform.

specs.maker: Several (Sony, Panasonic, Yamaha, Philips and others)

curiosities: The meaning of the name MSX has never been settled; explanations include "Machines with Software eXchangeability".
The Soviet Union installed Yamaha MSX computers in school classrooms.
In the Arab world, Sakhr sold MSX machines with Arabic-language support.
Its video chip is the same Texas Instruments family used in the ColecoVision and SG-1000.
story: Kazuhiko Nishi of ASCII and Microsoft Japan wanted one standard for home computers, as VHS was for video. Announced in 1983, MSX was a specification any maker could build: a Z80, a TI video chip, a General Instrument sound chip and Microsoft BASIC.

Sony, Panasonic, Philips, Toshiba, Yamaha and many others built MSX machines. They sold well in Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, Brazil and the Arab world, though not in Britain or America. Konami made its name on it with Metal Gear, Nemesis and Knightmare.
Millions of MSX computers were sold over the standard's four generations, and Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear first appeared on the MSX2.
